name: The Glass Bridge
unique_feature: a fused-stone Oroth bridge over a dry riverbed of black glass
story: The river was sung dry in the Ash Winter. The glass is the riverbed's last shape, and it is sharp.
encounter: ash-wights under the arch; the glass bed does bleed damage if you fight on it

name: The Pilgrims' Bell
unique_feature: a Hearthstone inside a fallen bell you enter through the crack in its side
story: The Order rings it once a day so the Choir knows it is still watched. Inside, the ringing goes on for an hour.

name: The Headless Watch
unique_feature: a colossus's fallen head hollowed into a watchtower, its eye the window
story: The Order keeps one knight in the eye at all times. The current one has been there eleven years and asks for news of Tollmere prices.
encounter: a fallen Tolling knight on the stair if the watch has turned; otherwise a friendly vigil

name: The One Poppy
unique_feature: a single red poppy in a square kilometre of grey grass
story: Nobody planted it and nothing eats it. Picking it is a deed the whole heath will know about by morning.
encounter: none; a Hollow deed if picked, a Hearth deed if watered

name: The Thirteenth
unique_feature: a thirteenth colossus lying face down far from the Choir's ring, as if it walked away
story: The Choir has twelve. This one has a head, buried in ash, and it is not the head of the others. A Sayer camp digs here and argues.
encounter: choristers around the excavation; casters whose note damages until silenced

name: The Cold Fire
unique_feature: ash-wights seated around a fire that went out a hundred and seventy years ago, still passing a cup
story: The people of Greyfold sat down to wait out the Ash Winter. They are still waiting, and they wave.
encounter: swarm; they only rise if you touch the cup

name: The Glass Falls
unique_feature: a dry waterfall of black glass, climbable, the shortcut up to the Choir plateau
story: Water still sounds here if you stand still. The Order forbids the climb and uses it themselves.
encounter: a bell-bearer at the top rings when it sees you; stun radius, break line of sight behind the glass ledges

name: The Hushline Stair
unique_feature: Oroth stairs descending into the mist where colour drains from your own hands
story: Where the Foundling walked out. Wren Tallow's Hearthstone at the top step is the first name you are given.
encounter: the tutorial: ash-wights on the stair; the mist turns you back below the fortieth step

name: The Stair Head
unique_feature: the Wardens' camp at the head of the Hushline Stair: a fire kept on the rim, grey-green colours on two poles, a lamp at the way out, and waystones walking north across the heath to the Choir
story: Where a new game hands over (DESIGN 5.1a). Wren Tallow keeps her fire here, above the Stair and out of the mist, and this is where she says the Foundling's name back. The position is the spot the Foundling stands on; the camp is laid out ahead of it, towards where its path leads.
encounter: none at the camp; the waystones keep more than fifty metres from anything the built world stands on the heath, and a test says which leg to move when a rebuild stands something nearer

name: The Sunk Plaza
unique_feature: a Builders' plaza sunk six steps into the ash, its fountain dry and full of little bells
story: Pilgrims drop a bell into the fountain on the way south, a habit older than the Order. The Order empties it into the chapter-house once a year and counts.
encounter: choristers sing in the plaza after dark
hook: The Order counts the fountain's bells every spring, and this year there is one more bell than there were pilgrims.

name: Bell Street
unique_feature: a street of the Builders' city lined with house-sized bells sunk to their shoulders in the ash
story: Each bell was a house, or a steeple, or both. Some are hollow and pilgrims shelter in them; one is not hollow, and hums.
encounter: ash-wights shelter in the hollow bells
hook: The bell that is not hollow: a Sayer wants it measured, the Order wants it left alone.

name: The Tower of Vaelost
unique_feature: an Oroth tower still standing over the Builders' city, its top course ringing faintly whenever wind crosses the heath
story: The tallest thing the Builders left in Cinderlea outside the Choir. The Sayers call it Vaelost, the kept one, and nobody has climbed it since its stair turned to glass.
encounter: a bell-bearer walks its round at the foot
hook: The top course has a name cut in it, and the Order will pay to know whose.

name: The Anthem Hall
unique_feature: a Builders' choir-school whose stone benches still face a singer who is not there
story: Anthe-Thael, the Sayers call it: the door of the choir. A whisper at the front is heard at the back as a shout, so pilgrims do not whisper in it.
hook: A lecture given here reaches the whole heath; the Circle would like to give one, and the Order would like them not to.

name: The Cistern of Isse
unique_feature: a Builders' cistern whose stair goes down into dry dark and sounds, all the way down, like water
story: The Builders stored water under their city and the Ash Winter drank it. The reedfolk say Isse of the Reeds walked up this stair out of the marsh, which is two regions away.
hook: Carry water from the Wellspring down the stair: something at the bottom wants to know whether it is still water.

name: The Kneeling Colossus
unique_feature: a fourteenth colossus kneeling on the rim with its hands over where its ears would be
story: The Choir has twelve and the Thirteenth walked away. This one stayed at the rim and covered its ears; the Order does not count it and will not say why.
hook: The Thirteenth's diggers want to dig this one too; the Order says a thing covering its ears has earned being left alone.

name: The Bell Garden
unique_feature: a Builders' garden of bells planted mouth-down in rows like cabbages, each a different note
story: When the Toll hums, the whole garden hums with it a half-note below, and the knights of the ring go and stand in the rows until it stops.
hook: Struck in the right order the garden plays a line, and the Cantor's Seat's door answers it.

name: Greywatch
unique_feature: three stones on the rim where the Order reads aloud the names of the ones who walked down
story: The Vigil Book says walk with them to the line. The line is below the rim; the stones are where the Order stops and reads, because a name read carries further than a walk.
hook: A name has been read at Greywatch every night for a month that is on no Chapter Roll.

name: The Ash-Winter Carts
unique_feature: a waystation roofless since the Ash Winter, its yard still full of the grain carts that were never unloaded
story: Then the roads west went under ash and the carts stopped coming. These are the carts: the grain is ash, the horses are bones in the traces, and the Order leaves them as they are.
hook: The carter's day-book lists a delivery to Greyfold made after the village had walked south.

name: The Bell Wood Stone
unique_feature: a Hearthstone in the White Wood, where pilgrims tie their bells to the dead ash trees before they walk south
story: Thousands of small bells hang in the dead wood and ring together in the dry wind. The pilgrims who tie them never come back for them, and nobody takes them down.
hook: Every bell in the wood is a person: the Wardens want the names written down, and the Order says the bells already are the names.

name: Ashcombe
unique_feature: a hamlet emptied in the Ash Winter whose chimneys still draw, though no fire has been lit in them for a hundred and seventy-seven years
story: Greyfold is remembered because of its tables. Ashcombe is not remembered at all, which is the worse end; the Wardens found it on an old tithe list and have not dared to put it back on the Roll.
encounter: ash-wights at the hearths after dark
hook: Put Ashcombe back on the Roll: find a name for each house, one chimney at a time.

name: Hesk Pool
unique_feature: Oroth steps going down into a still pool that gives back no reflection at all
story: Eelfathom Pool shows you a few seconds late; Hesk Pool does not show you at all. The Sayers call it the silence-water and take readings. Pilgrims do not look into it on the way south.
hook: The Sayers say Hesk Pool and Eelfathom are the same water, and that something stands in between.

name: The Last Milestone
unique_feature: three fused-stone milestones counting down to a harbour that is no longer there
story: The Builders' road west from the Choir ends in three markers: one, then none, then a stone with a word the Sayers read as shore. The sea is further west than that now.
hook: Walk the road the milestones count down and find the Builders' Harbour on the strand.

name: The Builders' Harbour
unique_feature: a Builders' quay whose steps go down into the Grey Sea and whose mooring posts are bells
story: Where the Builders' city met the sea. The Salt Isles traders would never moor here; they said the bells ring when a ship is coming that has not yet set out.
hook: The harbour bells rang last night; the reedfolk say a Salt Isles ship is due, and none has been seen in forty years.

name: The Grey Wreck
unique_feature: a Salt Isles salt-barge driven onto the Ash Strand and gone grey to the waterline
story: She came ashore in the Ash Winter with a hold of salt that had turned to ash on the voyage. Her crew walked inland and are on nobody's list.
encounter: ash-wights in the hold, still in their oilskins
hook: The barge's chart has the Salt Isles on it, and a line ruled from them to the Choir.

name: The Strand Beacon
unique_feature: a salt-traders' beacon of grey stone on the strand, its fire-bowl lit every night by nobody anyone has met
story: The Salt Isles traders built it to find the strand and stopped coming forty years ago. It burns every night anyway.
hook: Sit a night at the Strand Beacon and see who lights it.

name: The Ninth Waystone
unique_feature: three waystones on the road down from the West Downs with the Order's bell-count for every year scratched into them
story: Pilgrims coming down off the downs count the waystones. At the ninth they stop being Vale folk and start being pilgrims, and some of them sit on it for a while first.
hook: The bell-counts on the stone stop in 1024 and start again this spring, in a hand the Order does not know.

name: The Hermit's Gate
unique_feature: a Builders' gatehouse with a hermit's cell in its arch and a door with no hinges that he says he opened once
story: The hermit in the gate has lived on pilgrims' bread for thirty years. He is not mad, which is what makes people uneasy; he is waiting for the door to open again.
hook: The hermit says the door opens for a name, as the Undercroft's does, and he has been trying names for thirty years.

name: The Hush Bell
unique_feature: a bell-tower on the cliff's edge whose bell hangs out over the Hush on a stone arm
story: The pilgrims rang it for the ships that brought them. No ship has come since the Stair was cut, and the rope has rotted to a hand's length.
hook: The bell has been rung: the rope is new, and wet with sea-water.

name: The Tenth Waystone
unique_feature: a pilgrims' waystone with ten notches in its edge and a bowl worn in its top for coins
story: The waystones count on from the Vale toward the Choir, and the pilgrims leave a coin in each bowl. The tenth's is always empty by morning.
hook: The coins taken from the tenth waystone turn up in the fire at the Stair Head, melted.

name: The Row of Mouths
unique_feature: a colonnade of Oroth pillars, each carved as an open mouth, running west from the Choir into the ash
story: The Builders' processional way from the Choir to their city. The pilgrims walk it with their mouths shut.
encounter: choristers walk the colonnade at night
hook: At dusk one mouth is heard singing a single note, a different pillar every night, and the Order is counting which.

name: Hesk-Morn
unique_feature: an Oroth door with no hinges standing upright on the cliff's edge, opening on the Hush
story: The pilgrims call it the Silent Door and will not walk between it and the sea. The Order says the Builders stood in it to listen to the Hush.
hook: The door has been found open, and the ash beyond it holds footprints that walk out onto the air.

name: The Silent Market
unique_feature: a market square of the dead city with its stalls still standing in fused stone, the goods on them all ash
story: The pilgrims will not cross it by day and the Ashgrid's scavengers will not cross it by night. Nobody says what is sold there.
hook: One stall at the edge of the square has fresh goods on it every morning: bread, a knife, a child's shoe.

name: Sulion
unique_feature: the dead city's harbour light, its lamp-socket empty and staring out to sea
story: The Builders' harbour light. Its sul-stone is the one in the Lamp at Gullhithe, carried across Wickmere by Tallymen in 998 and never paid for.
hook: The empty socket glows on moonless nights, and on those nights the Lamp at Gullhithe dims.

name: The North Gate
unique_feature: the dead city's north gate, a fused-stone arch standing alone with no wall left either side of it
story: The pilgrims walk through it rather than round it; out of courtesy, the Order says.
hook: Something passes through the gate at the same hour every night, leaving the ash disturbed and no tracks.

name: The Greyline Stones
unique_feature: a line of chalk stones marking where the grey begins, each one set a little further back than the one before
story: The Wardens set a stone at the edge of the ash every Naming Day. Every year the ash has come a few yards on, and the new stone goes in behind it.
hook: This year's stone was set in front of last year's: the ash has gone back.

name: The Driftwood Camp
unique_feature: a strand-scavengers' camp roofed with driftwood and a ship's ribs
story: The Ash Strand's scavengers live off what the Grey Sea brings in, which is less every year.
hook: The sea brought in a Tollmere barge last week with her cargo sealed and her crew gone.

name: The Grey Hedge
unique_feature: a Vale farm's hedge gone grey in the White Wood, its hawthorns turned to ash-wood standing in their rows
story: The farm went grey in the Ash Winter and the house is gone. The hedge stands because nobody has told it.
hook: One hawthorn in the grey hedge has come into leaf.

name: The Bell Pit
unique_feature: a pit where the dead city's broken bells were buried, their rims showing through the ash
story: The Tolling Order buried every bell it could not hang, so that nobody would ring a broken one. There are two hundred in the pit.
encounter: bell-bearers dig in the pit at night
hook: One of the buried bells has been dug up in the night, hung from a dead tree, and rung once.

name: The Last Hearth
unique_feature: the last Hearthstone the Wardens keep on the grey side, its fire banked with chalk
story: The Wardens' patrols turn back here. The fire is kept so that the last thing a patrol sees of the ash is a Vale fire, and the first thing a pilgrim sees of the Vale.
hook: The chalk the fire is banked with has turned grey overnight, right through.

name: The Weighhouse
unique_feature: the dead city's weighhouse, its great scales fused solid with one pan down
story: The Tallymen have tried for a century to take the scales home. The Order says the pan is down because something was weighed here and found wanting.
hook: The scales have moved: the other pan is down now.

name: The Turning Cairn
unique_feature: a cairn of pilgrims' hand-bells on the last bend of the Stair Path, every clapper tied with grey thread
story: A pilgrim who goes down the Stair and comes back up again leaves the bell here, tied silent, and does not say why. The Order counts the bells each spring. The count has never gone down.
hook: One bell on the cairn has been untied, and it has been rung: the thread lies on the stones beside it, cut clean.

name: The Sweeper's Lean-To
unique_feature: a lean-to of pilgrims' staves by the Choir road, a fire, and a broom worn down to the binding
story: Arn Sweeting went down the Stair nineteen years ago, stood a night at the Hushline, and came back up. The Order has no rule for a pilgrim who comes back, so it lets him sweep the grey off the pilgrim road, and he keeps what the broom turns up.
encounter: none; the sweeper at his fire
hook: The broom turned up a hand-bell with a name scratched on it, and the name is not a pilgrim's.

name: The Novices' Seats
unique_feature: three seats cut in the plateau's lip over the Hush, their backs to the Choir, worn hollow by novices of the Order
story: A novice of the Tolling Order sits here a day and a night before anything else is taught, facing the grey with the Choir behind, and counts the bells without turning round. Those who turn round are sent home, kindly.
hook: One of the seats has been turned in the night to face the Choir, and it is a single stone the size of a cart.

name: The Tide Mouth
unique_feature: a sea-cave in the cliff foot west of the Landing, low to the water, where the grey comes in on the tide and goes out again clear
story: The Order says the Tide Mouth breathes the grey: it comes in grey on the flood and goes out clear on the ebb, and somewhere inside the cave keeps what the water leaves.
hook: The tide went out this morning and left a pilgrim's bell on the shell sand, clapper tied, with no name on it.

name: The Salt Road Cairn
unique_feature: a lone cairn on the grey heath where the salt-traders' road came up from the strand, each of its stones rimed white with old salt
story: The Salt Isles traders left a stone on the cairn going inland and took one back coming down to their boats, so the cairn stood a stone higher for every trader still ashore. They stopped coming forty years ago, and the cairn has been exactly as high since.
hook: A stone crusted with fresh salt has been added to the cairn, the first in forty years, and the Strand Beacon burned green that night.

name: The Last Meal Stone
unique_feature: a flat stone on the rim road where pilgrims eat their last meal as Vale folk before they go down, crusts and cups left round it
story: The pilgrims walking to the Choir stop being Vale folk at the Ninth Waystone and start being pilgrims, and at this stone they eat the last food they brought from home. What is left is left on the stone, and the knights of the ring clear it at dusk and say nothing. Nobody goes down to the Hush armed, and the pilgrims leave their weapons at the stone with the crusts; the knights of the ring let whoever needs one take it.
hook: Somebody has eaten a last meal at the stone every evening this month, and in the morning the plate is washed and set straight, and nobody new is on the Stair.

name: The Bowing Stones
unique_feature: three leaning stones on the Choir road beneath the Headless Watch, bent toward the Choir like the colossi bowing
story: The Builders set three stones where their procession first saw the Choir whole, and the stones have leaned toward it ever since, a little more every century, the way the pilgrims lean when they first see it themselves.
hook: The stones have leaned a hand further toward the Choir since the Toll began to hum, and the knight in the Headless Watch's eye has measured it.

name: The Scavengers' Cold Camp
unique_feature: an Ashgrid scavengers' camp on the Greyfold road; the fire went out and nobody relit it, and sacks of Builders' brass are left by the cold hearth
story: The Ashgrid's scavengers dig brass out of the dead city for Tollmere's foundries and camp in the lee of whatever wall stands. This camp was left all at once, with the brass still in the sacks, which a scavenger does not do. One of the sacks holds a pilgrim's ashen greatsword, dug out of the grid and never sold.
encounter: ash-wights wander the Greyfold road after dark
hook: Every piece of brass the scavengers left in their sacks has been polished bright in the night, as if for a feast.

name: The Robing-House
unique_feature: a Builders' robing-house beside the Anthem Hall, roofless, one gable standing, stone pegs down its walls for robes long gone to ash
story: The Builders' singers robed here before they went into the Anthem Hall, a peg for every singer, and the pegs are still there in rows. The pilgrims count them and count the Hall's benches, and the numbers match.
hook: Grey robes have been hung on the pegs, dry and newly woven and sized for children, one peg short of the Anthem Hall's benches.

name: The Harbour Milestone
unique_feature: a broken Oroth milestone on the harbour road, its top lying face-up at its foot, a ship cut on it and a count in Oroth numerals that nobody can read
story: The Builders' road from their city to their harbour was marked with stones, and this is the last one standing, or half standing. The Sayers read the numerals as a count of something, not a distance, and have argued for a century about what.
encounter: ash-wights walk the harbour road in the evening
hook: The count on the fallen top has gone down by one since spring.

name: The Half-Ash Cairn
unique_feature: a pilgrims' cairn on the western ash, half of black ash-stone and half of Vale chalk, where the grey began the year it was built
story: The Wardens built the cairn of chalk at the edge of the grey after the Ash Winter, and the pilgrims going to the West Walk have added ash-stones ever since, so the cairn has gone grey from the ground up, like the country.
hook: The cairn has been rebuilt in one night all of chalk again, white to the ground, and the grey round its foot has drawn back a stride.

name: The First-Step Cairn
unique_feature: a pilgrims' cairn on the ash heath off the Choir road, a wand of white ash stuck in its top with a strip of faded gold tied to it
story: Pilgrims who come up out of the Hushline, which nobody does, are meant to leave a stone here, the first thing a returning pilgrim touches that is not the Hush's. There are very few stones. There are more than there should be.
hook: A new stone was on the cairn on the morning the Foundling came up the Stair, and it was warm.

name: The Scavenger's Grave
unique_feature: a scavenger's grave in the Ashgrid by the Tower of Vaelost, a heap of fused stone with a bell on a stake at its head
story: The Ashgrid's scavengers bury their own where they fall, under the dead city's stone, with a bell on a stake the way the Order marks a pilgrim's last camp, because the wights leave a belled grave alone.
hook: The bell on the stake has been ringing on windless nights, and the scavengers say it is being rung from underneath.

name: The Salt Hulk
unique_feature: a salt-traders' trading ship run up on the Ash Strand and left, its ribs white with salt, a ladder still hung over the side
story: The salt-traders sailed to the strand from the Salt Isles when there was a Greyfold to sell to, and the last of their ships came in after the Toll and found nobody on the quay. The crew walked up the old salt road and did not come back for her.
hook: The ladder over the side is pulled up in the evening and let down again in the morning, and there has been nobody aboard for a hundred and seventy years.

name: The Tower-Road Bell
unique_feature: a pilgrims' shrine on the Tower of Vaelost road, a fallen bell set upright on three stones with a candle burned down inside it
story: Pilgrims who go down into the Ashgrid to see the Tower stop at the bell first. It fell from the Tower in the Toll and rolled here, and the Order set it upright where it stopped and has kept a candle burning under it ever since.
hook: The candle under the bell has been found lit every morning this month, and none of the pilgrims who pass will say they lit it.

name: The Warden Under the Ash
unique_feature: a pilgrims' grave on the West Walk, a mound of black ash stones with a bell on a stake at its head and a Warden's cloak-pin nailed to the stake
story: A Warden walked out along the West Walk after the Toll to see how far the grey went, and the pilgrims found him sitting against the stake that marked the road, dead and smiling. They buried him where he sat, their way, with a bell, and nailed his pin to the stake so the Wardens would know him.
hook: The cloak-pin on the stake has been polished bright, the Wardens' way, and there is no Warden posted on the West Walk.

name: The Glass-Road Stone
unique_feature: a waystone on the Greyfold road short of the Glass Bridge, its face scored with pilgrims' marks and a rumour scratched fresh along its top
story: The pilgrims mark the stone as they pass, one line each, to say they got this far. The top is kept for news: whatever the last one heard on the heath, scratched in for the next.
hook: The rumour on the stone's top says the Glass Bridge has been heard ringing underfoot, and it is in a hand the pilgrims know, a pilgrim who went down to the Choir a year ago.

name: Turnback Keep
unique_feature: a ruined five-sided keep of grey ashlar on the west heath, its drum towers broken, the names of everyone who kept its vigil cut round the inside of its gate-arch
story: The four who came back up the Stair in the Ash Winter, from the fortieth step, would not stand at the ring with the eleven who had stayed. They built this keep on the west heath with its gate towards the Choir and kept a count of their own here for a hundred years. Aveline Ash, the first of the four to turn, kept it until she died, and then went on keeping it; the Order left Turnback when its knights began to turn a second time, the wrong way, and took nothing with them.
encounter: fallen Tolling knights and ash-wights hold the walls; choristers on the towers; the First Vigilant under the keep, in the undercroft where the Turnback Count is kept
hook: Elsbet Ash, the last knight to leave Turnback, keeps a fire outside its gate and reads the names round the arch every evening, and asks whoever comes by to go down for the Turnback Count, a hundred years of bells the Order has never seen.

site.hook_prompt: Read the names round the gate-arch

name: The Salt Landing
unique_feature: a Salt Isles traders' camp on the grey heath above the strand, their boat hauled up on rollers, its sail rigged over the salt sacks, and a lantern hung on an oar for a ship that has not come in
story: The Salt Isles ships stopped coming forty years ago. This spring one boat came, rowed by a brother and a sister who had heard the Builders' Harbour bells ringing from the sea, and they have made a camp above the strand to trade salt for Oroth glass and wait for the ship that is supposed to follow them.
encounter: none; two Salt Isles traders at their fire
hook: The ship that should have followed the boat has not come, and the traders say Sulion's empty socket is showing a light on the wrong nights and drawing ships onto the Ash Strand.

name: The Bell-Counter's Hut
unique_feature: a hermit's shelter of ash boughs leant against a boulder on the open heath, the boulder's face scratched from the ground to its top with tallies of bells
story: Eddery Wray sat the Novices' Seats in 1024 and turned round, and was sent home kindly, and never went home. He has lived on the heath between the waystones ever since, counting the Choir's bells for nobody. He stopped writing his counts on the waystones when he was sent away. This spring the Toll hummed and he started again.
hook: The count on the boulder does not agree with the Order's: by his tally the Choir has rung one bell more this year than there are bells in the Choir.

name: The Bell-Rope Walk
unique_feature: a ropewalk on the cliff-top heath: a long file of trestles and posts where the Tolling Order lays the ropes for the Choir's bells, grey strands stretched fifty paces in the wind between a spinning-wheel and a weighted sledge
story: Every bell the Order rings hangs from a rope laid here, of flax carried up from the Vale and twisted in the ash wind, which the ropers say is what makes a bell-rope hold a note. Hewin Ash has laid the Order's ropes for thirty years. He counts his ropes the way the others count bells, and this spring he is one short.
encounter: none; the Order's roper at his wheel
hook: The rope that turned up new on the Hush Bell is one of Hewin's, and it is wet with sea-water, and the Hush Bell hangs over a cliff nobody climbs.

name: Greyfleece Shieling
unique_feature: a drystone shieling above the Ash Strand where the last flock on the grey side grazes the ash-grass, their fleeces grey to the root
story: The Tarrants kept sheep on Ashcombe's downs before the Ash Winter, and one of them stayed when the rest walked south. His sheep went grey and so did his great-granddaughter's, and Morwen Tarrant says grey wool takes no dye and wears for ever and the Order will buy all she can shear.
encounter: none; the shepherd and her flock
hook: Morwen has heard from a Warden that a hawthorn in the Grey Hedge has come into leaf, and she wants a cutting of it for the shieling wall before the grey takes it back.

name: Ashcombe Mill
unique_feature: Ashcombe's windmill on its low rise, its four sails still turning in the ash wind and grinding nothing, the millstones worn hollow
story: Ashcombe ground its corn here. When the village went quiet the mill did not, and the Wardens who found Ashcombe on the old tithe list found the sails turning and the miller and his boy still at the hopper, feeding ash between the stones.
encounter: the miller and his boy, ash-wights, at the stones; they only turn on you if you stop the sails
hook: The mill's sack-tally is still kept, in chalk on the door, a line for every sack; the last line was chalked this week.

name: The Scavengers' Ring
unique_feature: a low drystone ring on the Ashgrid's buried streets where the dead city's scavengers camp, their sieves and bronze scrap piled in the yard and a Builders' roof-boss for a hearth
story: The Ashgrid's scavengers dig down through the ash to the Builders' rooftops for bronze, glass and anything the Tallymen will buy. The Order does not like it and does not stop it. Coll Brisket has run the Ring for eleven years and lost nobody to the dead city in all that time, until this month.
encounter: none; the scavengers in their ring
hook: Three of Coll's diggers went down the new shaft west of the Ring and did not come up, and in the evenings the shaft sings.

name: The Rooftop Shaft
unique_feature: a scavengers' shaft sunk through the ash onto the roof of a buried Builders' hall, a timber headframe over it and a ladder going down into a sound like a held note
story: Coll Brisket's diggers sank this shaft in the spring and broke through a Builders' roof into a hall the ash had kept whole: a choir-school under the Ashgrid, the Sayers say, Anthe-Ondr, the Under-Choir. The first night the shaft stood open the scavengers heard it singing, and three of them went down to see.
encounter: choristers and ash-wights in the halls below; the Precentor in the singing-hall at the bottom
hook: A digger's tally-stick hangs from the headframe with three notches cut in it and a fourth begun.

name: The Unrung Graves
unique_feature: a pilgrims' burying ground in the dead city's west quarter, each grave marked with a hand-bell on a post, every clapper taken out
story: Pilgrims who died on the heath before they reached the Stair were buried here by the Order, with their bells, and the clappers were taken out so that nobody would ring a dead pilgrim's bell by mistake. The clappers are in the chapter-house at Pilgrim's Ash, in a box, each tied to a name.
encounter: a chorister walks the rows at dusk and sings the names
hook: One grave's bell has a name on it that the Order's box of clappers does not have.

name: The Sayers' Gauge
unique_feature: a Sayers' survey tower on the west heath, stairs running round its outside to a platform with a brass gauge on a tripod, trained on the edge of the grey
story: The Circle put up the Gauge in 1011 to measure how fast the grey was coming. Every year the Surveyor takes the readings, every year the grey has come further, and every year the Circle files them. This year Idrin Fenn has taken them three times, because they say the grey has gone back.
encounter: none; the Circle's surveyor at the gauge
hook: The Surveyor's readings say the grey has gone back, and she wants three other measures of it before she will write that down for the Circle.

name: The Last Furrow
unique_feature: a Greyfold farmstead west of the village, roofless, its yard grey, and in its field a plough-team of wights still ploughing the furrow they began the morning the ash came down
story: The Hallows farmed Greyfold's west field and were ploughing it the morning the Ash Winter began. Greyfold walked south singing at noon. The Hallows had not finished the furrow, and they are ploughing it still, a hundred and seventy-seven years long.
encounter: the Hallows at the plough, ash-wights; they leave you be until you stand in the furrow
hook: The furrow is nearly at the headland. The Order would like to know what the Hallows will do when it is finished.
